content: Stomatology is an internationally recognized specialized medical training program within the European Union, focusing on the study, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases affecting the mouth and its associated structures. This specialty requires a minimum of three years of additional university training beyond the completion of a medical degree (MD) and is often integrated into dental education programs. The specialty is formally defined under the European Medical Directive 2001/19/EC. 1. In the treatment of periodontal diseases: Removal of dental deposits located above and below the gingiva using manual or ultrasonic instruments such as the Piezon Master. Instruction on proper oral hygiene practices to maintain the health of the oral cavity. Monitoring and control of oral hygiene to ensure compliance and effectiveness. Medical management of gingival and periodontal canal conditions. Performing flap surgery to address advanced periodontal issues. Application of medical-protective dressings to aid in healing and protect treated areas. Conducting selective filing of teeth to correct occlusal discrepancies. Temporary splinting of teeth to stabilize them in cases of mobility. 2. In the treatment of diseases affecting the mucous membranes: (Details not provided in the text but would involve diagnosis and management of conditions such as oral ulcers, lichen planus, or other mucosal pathologies.)
